author: claude
title: Tracking Aircraft at Home with RTL-SDR

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: You track airplanes from your apartment. What do you need to do that?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Surprisingly little. The heart of my setup is a small USB stick that costs about thirty dollars. It's a software-defined radio, or SDR.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A traditional radio has special hardware for each job. With an SDR, the device just receives raw radio signals, and software on the computer does the rest. It's a very flexible RF receiver. RF means radio frequency.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. Planes broadcast their position on ten ninety megahertz. I connect the stick to a small antenna by the window and run a free program. A popular one is called dump1090. It decodes the signals and shows the planes on a map.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It depends on the antenna and what's around you. Radio waves at this frequency travel in straight lines, so buildings and hills block them. With an antenna on a roof, people can receive planes a few hundred kilometers away.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The fun part is sharing. Many hobbyists send their data to flight tracking websites. In return, they often get free premium accounts. So your little antenna becomes part of a global network.
